messages:
Aisha P: Heads-up — Skyline onboarding: their Node SDK init is spiking 429s and we also see lots of ephemeral session tokens being created instead of reused. Seeing customer churn risk if we don't stabilize this.
Sam K: Can you paste the minimal repro logs? 429s during init usually means preflight/concurrency fanout.
Aisha P: Pasting console log snippet they sent:
```
[2025-06-02T15:10:22Z] GET /v1/auth/preflight 200 12ms
[2025-06-02T15:10:22Z] POST /v1/sessions 201 8ms session_id=abc123
[2025-06-02T15:10:22Z] POST /v1/sessions 201 6ms session_id=def456
[2025-06-02T15:10:22Z] POST /v1/generate 429 2ms error=rate_limit
```
Jules R: Looks like their client is calling session creation for every user request. We recommend reusing the session token (TTL 30m) and doing client-side pooling. Did they implement ephemeral token caching?
Aisha P: They said they call createSession() in middleware on every request because they assumed sessions are single-use.
Maya L: @Sam K, can we confirm server-side behavior — are session endpoints counted against the same rate bucket as generate requests? I think session creation is accounted separately but preflight + session + generate in quick succession can trip the per-minute window.
oncall-bot: Rate limit window: 60s, bucket=api:per_key:minute
Sam K: Confirmed — session creation and generate share the customer's global unit bucket; we count all write-like requests. If their app fanouts 10 parallel requests per page load, that explains the 429s.
Aisha P: Customer is on a mid-tier plan with default burst allowance. They ramped test traffic from a small QA cohort to 150 concurrent clients.
Jules R: Quick mitigation steps to propose to Skyline: 1) Cache session token in client (reuse for TTL), 2) Implement exponential backoff with jitter for 429s, 3) Pre-warm with a single session per browser tab, 4) Consider reducing preflight calls by reusing preflight results.
Aisha P: I'll draft an email with sample code. Want a short code snippet we can give them for Node SDK caching.
Maya L: Use this snippet (pseudo):
```js
// minimal session cache
const sessionCache = new Map();
async function getSession(userId){
  if (sessionCache.has(userId)) return sessionCache.get(userId);
  const s = await sdk.createSession({user: userId});
  sessionCache.set(userId, s);
  setTimeout(()=> sessionCache.delete(userId), 25*60*1000); // keep < TTL
  return s;
}
```
Sam K: Also mention server-side rate limits: advise them to aggregate background calls (batch requests) and avoid creating sessions in synchronous hot paths.
Aisha P: I'll send email with snippet + ask them to run a 30-min soak at 20 concurrent clients and report 429 rate. If persistent, we can temporarily bump their burst allocation while they refactor.
Jules R: +1. If they want immediate relief, we can grant a 2x short-lived burst for 24h but will need support approval.
Aisha P: @Sam K can you flag to support for a temporary burst and include the logs above?
Sam K: Flagging support; ticket created #SUP-10244. I'll include the logs and recommended config.
Aisha P: Great — I'll loop in Skyline engineering and propose the steps. Thanks team :thumbsup:
Maya L: Optional: add client-side circuit breaker to avoid thundering herd on reconnects (in case mobile clients restart).
Aisha P: Noted. I'll add that to the action items.
